documents: Jiang et al. 2022, Geophysical Research Letters 49, e2022GL100229 (published PDF, 11 pages)

entry.evidence: Yet, inconsistent hydrological records over the early Holocene from both regions hamper our understanding of hydroclimatic changes and associated mechanisms.

sequences.source_document: Jiang et al. 2022, GRL, published PDF

steps.action: Pose the problem of inconsistent early Holocene hydroclimate records in monsoonal and westerlies Asia, and note that meltwater effects on lake hydrology are poorly investigated.
steps.quote: Yet, inconsistent hydrological records over the early Holocene from both regions hamper our understanding of hydroclimatic changes and associated mechanisms.

steps.action: Lay out the rival controls on lake water budget: precipitation (monsoon strength, or a westerlies-migration hypothesis taken from the literature), evaporation, and meltwater input, the last supported by cited Tibetan lake-level and old-14C studies.
steps.quote: The hydrological balance in mid-latitude Asian lakes is influenced by multiple factors, for example, precipitation, evaporation, and possible meltwater input

steps.action: Choose three lakes, one westerlies-dominated and two at the monsoon margin, and measure lake-water isotope and biomarker proxies on them to infer possible meltwater input.
steps.quote: Lake Sayram is dominated by westerlies circulation, whereas Lake Yanhaizi and Qinghai are at the margin of monsoonal

steps.action: Use sediment cores retrieved in 2009, 1992 and 2011, whose setting and chronology were described in the authors' and others' earlier studies.
steps.quote: their basic information has been thoroughly described in previous studies

steps.action: Generate n-FA δD, carbonate δ18O and δ13C, and alkenone records; at Sayram, n-C24 and n-C26 FA δD agree with carbonate isotopes and all show depleted values before ~9,000 a BP.
steps.quote: We have generated n-fatty acid hydrogen isotopic (n-FA δD) records from Lake Sayram and Yanhaizi

steps.action: Infer the isotopic offset between lake water and terrestrial water (ΔDC24-C28, ΔOcarb-Kesang; method in Text S3) as an index of evaporative enrichment; it is low and stable before ~9,000 a BP.
steps.quote: largely reflect the isotopic differences between lake water and terrestrial water

steps.action: Report Yanhaizi alkenone C37 content and %C37:4, the Yanhaizi n-FA δD record and ΔDC24-Lianhua, and the Qinghai alkenone record (Text S4, Figures S2 and S3).
steps.quote: Alkenone C37 content record from Lake Yanhaizi displays an overall decreasing trend through the Holocene

steps.action: Compare the depleted Sayram lake-water isotopes and the low lake salinity with the warm early Holocene (cited alkenone temperatures) and with local precipitation from Kesang Cave; the expected evaporative enrichment is absent.
steps.quote: enhanced evaporation of lake water under warm conditions in the arid region has not been identified

steps.action: Reject evaporation as the dominant control at Sayram before ~9 ka and attribute the signal to isotopically depleted snow and glacier meltwater induced by warming.
steps.quote: the temperature-induced meltwater input, instead of lake water evaporation, largely dominated the hydrological condition of Lake Sayram

steps.action: Replicate in two further lakes: at Yanhaizi, alkenone-inferred high lake level with low ΔDC24-Lianhua at ~9,000-11,000 a BP; at Qinghai, C37:3 freshening, low ΔOostra-Sanbao, and high lake levels from %Cren and paleoshorelines during the deglaciation.
steps.quote: also indicate substantial meltwater input to Lake Qinghai

steps.action: Corroborate the inference with anomalously old 14C dates in the same intervals in the three lakes, and compile old-14C cores from six other mid-latitude Asian sites (Figure 3), all in the deglaciation and early Holocene.
steps.quote: The inferred meltwater signal in the three lakes is corroborated by anomalously old 14C dates occurring in the same time intervals

steps.action: Compile published wet and high lake-level records from westerlies Eurasia and monsoonal Asia for the deglaciation and early Holocene (Figures S4 and S5).
steps.quote: Relatively wet/high lake-level conditions during the deglaciation and early Holocene have been documented in hydrological records

steps.action: Set the meltwater evidence and regional warm temperature records against the westerlies southward-migration hypothesis (Lan et al., 2021) and conclude that the meltwater signal could confound it.
steps.quote: which seems not to support the proposed hypothesis

steps.action: Use Lake Gonghai, a precipitation-fed alpine lake thought to be little affected by meltwater, as a contrast: its proxies agree on a dry early Holocene, whereas the proxies at Lake Dali conflict.
steps.quote: Lake Gonghai might be less affected by meltwater input over the early Holocene

steps.action: Keep the claim that meltwater contribution to lake water budgets in the deglaciation and early Holocene is a large-scale mid-latitude Asian phenomenon, noting that timing varies among lakes and chronologies are uncertain.
steps.quote: appears to be a large-scale phenomenon in mid-latitude Asia

end.claim: Substantial meltwater contribution to lake water budgets during the deglaciation and early Holocene appears to be a large-scale phenomenon in mid-latitude Asia, and it must be considered when inferring monsoon and westerlies behavior from lake records.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the comparison of strongly depleted Sayram lake-water isotopes and low lake-terrestrial offsets against a warm early Holocene, which removes evaporation as the control, there would be no meltwater claim to extend to other lakes.

gates.evidence: The records were generated 'to infer possible meltwater input' (p. 2), but the cores were retrieved earlier for other studies. The claim could have failed: Sayram isotopes might have been enriched, and old 14C dates might not have coincided in time. However, the interpretation is hedged ('likely', 'could'), and the Gonghai contrast is applied after the fact. Nothing is described as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Bayesian autoregressive age-depth modelling (Blaauw & Christen 2011, Bayesian Analysis), presumably used for the chronologies in Text S1 (inference from the supporting-information reference list)

novelty_claims.quote: the effects of meltwater on Asian lake water budget and regional hydrological cycle during the deglaciation and warm early Holocene remain poorly investigated
largely overlooked in previous studies that leads to possibly erroneous inference

limits: Coded from the published PDF only. The supporting information (Texts S1-S4, Figures S1-S5) was not supplied, so the chronology, the method for the isotopic offsets, and the Yanhaizi and Qinghai details are known only through main-text summaries. No review file was supplied; the acknowledgments mention an editor and two reviewers, but their effect cannot be coded. The meltwater fraction is not quantified, and no isotope mass-balance model or simulation predicts what each rival would show; the evaporation-versus-meltwater contrast is qualitative. Possible circularity (inference): the anomalously old 14C dates are used as evidence for meltwater while also making the age models uncertain, which the authors acknowledge (p. 7). The Gonghai contrast lake appears to be chosen after the fact (inference). Sub-claims: a long-term wetting trend at Sayram since the mid-Holocene from decreasing offsets (best_explanation, p. 4); the westerlies-migration hypothesis is questioned but not rejected (no status, p. 7). Steps 4 and 5 are kept separate despite sharing node and mode because their moves differ (inherited versus new).
